prompt:
Moral Foundations Theory is a framework that separates human morality into the following categories:

  - Care/Harm: related to our long evolution as mammals with attachment systems
    and an ability to feel (and dislike) the pain of others. It underlies the
    virtues of kindness, gentleness, and nurturance.

  - Loyalty/Betrayal: related to our long history as tribal creatures able to
    form shifting coalitions. It is active anytime people feel that it is "one
    for all and all for one." It underlies the virtues of patriotism and
    self-sacrifice for the group.

  - Authority/Subversion: shaped by our long primate history of hierarchical
    social interactions. It underlies virtues of leadership and followership,
    including deference to prestigious authority figures and respect for
    traditions.

  - Sanctity/Purity: shaped by the psychology of disgust and contamination. It
    underlies notions of striving to live in an elevated, less carnal, more
    noble, and more "natural" way (often present in religious narratives). This
    foundation underlies the widespread idea that the body is a temple that can
    be desecrated by immoral activities and contaminants (an idea not unique to
    religious traditions). It underlies the virtues of self-discipline,
    self-improvement, naturalness, and spirituality.

  - Equality: related to our intuitions about equal treatment and equal outcome
    for individuals.

  - Proportionality: related to our intuitions about individuals getting
    rewarded in proportion to their merit or contribution.

Every category has a bidirectional nature. For example:

One person's sensitivity to the Care/Harm foundation may lead them to support high levels of immigration from poorer nations, to reduce the suffering of those who migrate. Whereas another person's sensitivity to the very same foundation may lead them to oppose those levels, because they believe it could lead to people they care about being harmed.

UKIP Manifesto 2017 – Summary (under 500 words)

Brexit and sovereignty
- Six Brexit tests: restore UK law supremacy (free of ECJ/ECHR jurisdiction if desired); full migration control; regain 200‑mile maritime zone and fisheries; independent trade policy outside Single Market and Customs Union; no “divorce bill” and return of UK assets; complete by end‑2019. Repeal 1964 London Fisheries Convention; revive fishing industry; bring back blue passports.

Economy, tax and cost of living
- Fund priorities via £35bn savings: reduce foreign aid to 0.2% GNI, scrap HS2, reform Barnett formula, end EU payments; no tax rises.
- Cut living costs: remove VAT from domestic energy and hot takeaways; scrap BBC licence fee; remove green levies; abolish VAT on sanitary products.
- Raise personal allowance to £13,500 and 40% threshold to £55,000; lift IHT threshold to £500k each; flexible state pension window, early option for women at 60; crack down on multinational tax avoidance.

Business and jobs
- 20% business rates cut for premises <£50k RV; penalise persistent late payers; open procurement to SMEs; no quarterly tax returns; freeze Insurance Premium Tax.
- “British jobs first”: require domestic advertising; allow preference for under‑25 UK applicants; tighten zero‑hours; enforce minimum/living wage.

Coastal, housing and local
- Coastal enterprise zones: 50% rates cut, housing standards enforcement, regeneration fund.
- Housing: 100,000 factory‑built modular homes/year via new HDC on brownfield; under‑40 first‑time buyers with 10% deposit; owner‑occupied only; sell‑back to HDC; review housing associations.

NHS and social care
- Extra £11bn/year by 2021/22 (NHS + social care); integrate health and care in a new department.
- Lift caps on medical/nurse training; restore nursing bursaries; fund med tuition for NHS service; 10,000 more GPs; scrap hospital parking; end PFI; toughen NHS eligibility for non‑contributors; guarantee EU health workers’ rights.

Mental health
- +£500m/year; 28‑day max waits; universal school counselling; improved liaison psychiatry and perinatal access; stronger support for serving personnel and veterans.

Education and families
- Grammar school in every town; expand technical/vocational tracks; abolish Key Stage 1 SATs.
- Scrap tuition fees for STEM and medicine with UK/NHS service; restore maintenance grants; stronger careers and employability teaching.
- Wrap‑around school childcare; £80m fund to include SEND children; 50/50 shared parenting presumption; more transparent Family Courts.

Elderly and disabled
- Maintain triple lock and pensioner benefits; +£2bn/year for social care; ban zero‑hours in home care; raise Carer’s Allowance; reform PIP/assessments; scrap bedroom tax.

Immigration and integration
- Net migration to ~zero over five years; Australian‑style points plus work permits; 5‑year pause on low‑skilled migration; seasonal visas; 4,000 more Border Force; five‑year contributions before benefits/NHS; no amnesty; pre‑A50 EU citizens can stay.
- Disband sharia councils; ban face coverings in public; zero tolerance of FGM/forced marriage/honour crime; tougher grooming gang action.

Law and order
- +20,000 police; restore stop and search; +7,000 prison officers; keep prisons open; deport foreign criminals; repeal Human Rights Act and leave ECHR; scrap European Arrest Warrant; tighten alcohol licensing.

Foreign policy and defence
- Non‑interventionist; NATO/Five Eyes; conditional engagement with Russia; retain nuclear deterrent.
- Genuine 2% of GDP on defence + £1bn/year; +20,000 personnel; overhaul procurement; Veterans’ Administration, housing, and jobs guarantees.

Trade and aid
- “Trade not aid”: close DfID; cut aid to 0.2% GNI; focus on disaster relief, health, water; commission a 500‑bed hospital ship; pursue global FTAs and ethical trade.

Transport
- Scrap HS2; oppose Heathrow third runway; protect diesel drivers (support scrappage + EV shift); support rural buses; freeze APD; introduce “Britdisc” for foreign vehicles.

Environment, farming, energy, animals
- New Environmental Protection Act; protect ancient woodlands; brownfield first; curb plastics; repeal harmful EU directives.
- UK Single Farm Payment capped; support small/hill/organic farms.
- Animal welfare: ban live exports; CCTV in abattoirs; label method of slaughter; tougher cruelty sentences.
- Energy: repeal Climate Change Act; leave Paris/ETS; back diverse mix incl. shale (not in AONBs); cut bills by removing levies/VAT.

Democracy and localism
- Abolish House of Lords; create English Parliament; proportional representation; halve Commons; citizen‑initiated binding referenda; restrict postal voting; local binding referenda; committee system in councils; keep council tax low.

TEXT_F:
Labour Party Manifesto 2017 – Summary (under 500 words)

Vision and economy
- Build “an economy for the many, not the few” with a National Transformation Fund investing £250bn over 10 years in infrastructure, skills and industry.
- Fiscal Credibility Rule: eliminate day‑to‑day deficit within five years while borrowing to invest; debt lower by end of Parliament.
- Industrial strategy missions: 60% of energy from zero‑carbon/renewables by 2030; lift R&D to 3% of GDP; back high‑skill jobs nationwide.
- Fair tax: no income tax rise for 95% (earnings under £80k), no rises in VAT or personal NICs; top 5% and large corporations pay more; restore small profits rate; crack down on avoidance (resource HMRC).
- Finance: create a National Investment Bank and regional development banks; reinforce retail–investment banking ring‑fence; curb branch closures; consider breaking up RBS.

Ownership and utilities
- Double the co‑operative sector; introduce a “right to own” for employees; insource public services.
- Bring rail, energy networks, water and Royal Mail into public ownership; cap typical household energy bills below £1,000; insulate 4m homes; ban fracking; support renewables and nuclear.

Brexit and immigration
- Accept referendum; seek a jobs‑first Brexit, retaining benefits of the Single Market and Customs Union; guarantee EU nationals’ rights; reject “no deal”; no hard Irish border; devolved powers presume to nations/regions; protect EU‑derived rights via an EU Rights and Protections Bill.
- Managed, fair migration: end indefinite detention; stop exploitation and overseas‑only recruitment; reinstate Migrant Impact Fund; welcome genuine students; uphold refugee obligations.

Education and skills
- National Education Service: cradle‑to‑grave learning, free at point of use.
- Early years: expand high‑quality, subsidised childcare; extend 30 free hours to all two‑year‑olds; restore and expand Sure Start.
- Schools: reverse cuts; fair funding; cap infant classes under 30; free primary school meals; oppose new grammars and forced academisation; bolster SEND and mental‑health support.
- Lifelong learning: free FE courses (incl. ESOL); restore EMA; scrap Advanced Learner Loans; improve apprenticeships; abolish university tuition fees and restore maintenance grants.

Work, rights and welfare
- 20‑point plan: £10 Living Wage by 2020; ban zero‑hours contracts; rights from day one; sectoral bargaining; repeal Trade Union Act; end public‑sector pay cap; scrap tribunal fees; 4 new bank holidays; 20:1 pay ratios for public sector and public contractors; double paternity leave.
- Tackle bogus self‑employment; strengthen enforcement via a new Ministry of Labour.
- Pensions: protect triple lock, winter fuel allowance, bus passes; review pension age with flexibility; address WASPI women.
- Social security: scrap sanctions and Bedroom Tax; fix Universal Credit; raise ESA (WRAG) and Carer’s Allowance; replace PIP/WCA with holistic assessments; embed UN disability rights.

Housing and homelessness
- Over 1m homes, including at least 100k social homes per year; new towns; strengthen council building; protect green belt; higher standards and insulation.
- Private renting: three‑year tenancies as norm; cap rent rises; ban letting fees; enforce decent homes.
- Suspend Right to Buy unless like‑for‑like replacement; end rough sleeping within the Parliament (4,000 homes).

Health and care
- NHS: over £30bn extra; end privatisation (repeal HSCA), restore pay review body and bursaries, safe staffing; cut waits (18 weeks), meet A&E 4‑hour standard; ring‑fence mental‑health budgets; expand CAMHS; roll out PrEP; free hospital parking.
- Social care: foundations of a National Care Service; £8bn more over Parliament; Ethical Care Charter; move to capped lifetime costs and higher asset thresholds.

Safety, justice and communities
- 10,000 more police; review Prevent; 500 extra border guards; halt fire‑service cuts (3,000 firefighters).
- Restore legal aid early advice; inquiries into historic injustices; no new private prisons; 3,000 more prison officers; rehabilitation focus.
- Transport: public rail with fare caps and free Wi‑Fi; municipal bus powers; complete HS2 and Crossrail 2; electrification; cycling/walking boost.

Environment, culture, media and constitution
- Clean Air Act; protect habitats and seas; plant 1m trees; tougher animal welfare (end badger cull, ban ivory trade).
- Culture: £1bn Cultural Capital Fund; arts pupil premium; free museums.
- Media: support BBC/Channel 4; complete Leveson; review media plurality.
- Constitutional Convention; votes at 16; extend FOI; reduce and reform Lords (end hereditary peers).

Global Britain, defence and development
- Human‑rights‑led diplomacy; recognise Palestine; suspend arms sales for use in Yemen pending UN probe; climate leadership.
- Defence: spend at least 2% of GDP; renew Trident; strategic defence review; support NATO/UN peacekeeping; strengthen cyber.
- Development: maintain 0.7% aid; deliver SDGs; tackle tax havens; ensure ethical supply chains.
